primitives.name: Immediate Space Intuition Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: My space-intuitions occur not in two times but in one.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{I}: \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{T}, \quad \mathcal{I}(s) = \tau \text{ where } \tau \in \mathcal{T} \text{ is the immediate topological form of } s
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{S}: sensory fiber space (dimensionless); \mathcal{T}: space of topological forms (dimensionless); \mathcal{I}: immediate intuition operator (dimensionless); \tau: topological form (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Sensory input carries topological structure natively; no intermediate 'inextensive sensation' stage; color and form are co-immediate in the same sensory fiber.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when sensory input is degraded below topological discrimination threshold (e.g., uniform ganzfeld, blindness); fails for abstract spaces lacking sensory correlate.

layer2.mapping: GSI: \mathcal{I} is the likelihood encoder p(\tau|s) with unit Jacobian (information-preserving). GSE: Single-timestep state transition s_t \to \tau_t with no hidden intermediate state.
layer2.telemetry: Psychophysical threshold for form-color simultaneity; fMRI latency between V1 and LOC for form vs color processing.

primitives.name: Intellectual Inweaving Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: They inweave the space-sensations with intellectual relations ; but these relations are the samne when they obtain between the elements of the space-system as when they obtain between any of the other elements of which the world is made.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{W}: \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{R} \to \mathcal{M}, \quad \mathcal{W}(\tau, \mathcal{R}) = \mu \text{ where } \mathcal{R} = \{\text{add, subtract, compare, measure, reproduce, abstract}\} \text{ are domain-general relations}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{T}: topological forms (dimensionless); \mathcal{R}: set of intellectual relations (dimensionless operators); \mathcal{M}: metric space representations (dimensionless); \mathcal{W}: inweaving operator (dimensionless); \mu: metric representation (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Intellectual relations \mathcal{R} are domain-general (apply equally to space, time, number, etc.); inweaving is a functorial action preserving relational structure; metric structure emerges from relational closure over topological primitives.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when relations \mathcal{R} are applied inconsistently (non-associative comparison, non-commutative addition); fails for non-archimedean or non-metric topologies where measurement relations break down.

layer2.mapping: GSI: \mathcal{W} implements conformal prediction set construction — intellectual relations define nonconformity scores. GSE: Multi-step reasoning chain where each relation application is a state transition \mu_{k+1} = r_k(\mu_k).
layer2.telemetry: Cross-domain transfer of spatial reasoning to numerical reasoning (fMRI adaptation); developmental trajectory of conservation tasks (Piaget).

primitives.name: Piecemeal Space Construction Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Most of us apprehend it in the barest symbolic abridgment: and if perchance we ever do try to make it more adequate, we just add one image of sensible extension to another until we are tired.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathbb{N}: iteration count (dimensionless); \mathcal{E}: space of sensible extension images (dimensionless); \epsilon_i: i-th extension image (dimensionless); \mathcal{P}: piecemeal construction operator (dimensionless); n: finite truncation (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Infinite unitary space is not an intuition but a symbolic limit; construction is additive concatenation of finite sensible extensions; process terminates at cognitive fatigue bound n_max.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails at n \to \infty (actual infinite not constructible); fails when extensions \epsilon_i are incompatible (non-embeddable); fails for non-Euclidean global topology not approximable by local Euclidean patches.

layer2.mapping: GSI: \mathcal{P} is a particle filter approximating the Kantian unitary space prior — particles are sensible extensions, weight degeneracy = fatigue. GSE: Iterative belief expansion with computational budget constraint; each \epsilon_i is a simulation rollout.
layer2.telemetry: Working memory span for spatial integration tasks; error growth in mental map stitching (closure error vs path length).

primitives.name: Asymmetric Spatial Resolution Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: And the space represented as near to us seems more minutely subdivisible than that we think of as lying far away.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{M}: metric representation (dimensionless); d: egocentric distance (meters); \alpha: resolution decay exponent (dimensionless); \rho: local subdivision resolution (subdivisions/meter); \mathcal{A}: asymmetric resolution operator (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Representational resolution decays with egocentric distance; near space has higher metric granularity; front/back asymmetry induces topological dropout (quote 11).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails at d=0 (singularity); fails for d > horizon where representation drops out entirely; fails for non-egocentric (allocentric) frames where asymmetry rotates.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Distance-dependent likelihood precision \rho(d) — conformal prediction sets widen with distance. GSE: State-dependent observation noise; near-space states have higher observability rank.
layer2.telemetry: Vernier acuity vs eccentricity; spatial memory precision decay with distance; foveal vs peripheral cortical magnification factor.

Asymmetric resolution \mathcal{A} reveals the representation is egocentrically warped: near space has higher metric granularity (\rho \propto d^{-\alpha}), far space drops out. Failure modes: \mathcal{I} breaks at sensory threshold; \mathcal{W} breaks at relational inconsistency; \mathcal{P} breaks at infinite limit; \mathcal{A} breaks at d=0 and horizon.
